text.p: Nigerians began registering on Monday for elections forming part of the military government's controversial programme to transfer to civilian rule.
The electoral commission says it expects to register about 50 million voters in Africa's most populous nation of about 100 million in an exercise that will last 10 days.
At St. Peter's registration centre on Ajele street in central Lagos, more than 150 people had registered within two hours of the opening.
"I'm registering because I want to make sure there is a change of government next year," said Ade Eniola, a young man on a queue of about 30 persons.
The head of the centre said the exercise had gone smoothly so far.
Nigeria's last attempt at democracy ended in chaos when the previous military ruler annulled a presidential vote in 1993.

General Sani Abacha, who seized power in the aftermath of the annulment has promised to hand over to an elected president next year but his critics say the transtition programme is a ruse to perpetuate himself in power.
Political observers said the registration of voters was crucial to the success of local council polls set for next month and the presidential election due in the third quarter of 1998.
